summary: Background eviction wave causing regional dedicated throughput sag and unfair GPU reservation
description:
Issue summary:
A sustained background eviction wave was observed in the eu-west dedicated pool during a midday customer window. The allocator began issuing accelerated evictions for long-lived prefetched KV caches on a subset of nodes which in turn triggered batcher starvation and a visible throughput sag for multiple dedicated customers. Impacted tenants saw increased p50/p99 generation latency and intermittent 5xx attach errors.

Impact:
- BrightDocs (dedicated customer) reported ~30% throughput drop and p99 increase from 400ms to ~1.6s for batched routes.
- Multiple small-tenant routes experienced fallback to lower-capacity variants.
- Autoscaler did not provision additional nodes for ~6 minutes due to suppressed attach telemetry from evicted slots.

Environment:
- prod (eu-west), reserved dedicated pool id: dp-eu-09
- Affected model footprints: 13B q4 and 6.7B quantized variants

Observed behavior:
- Rapid sequence of eviction events correlated with snapshotter GC cycles and a prefetched KV cache flush on a subset of nodes.
- Allocator log shows accelerated eviction decisions followed by many short-lived attach attempts and slot churn.
- Autoscaler metrics show muted attach signals and then an overshoot when attach telemetry resumed.

Expected behavior:
- Prefetch/GC activity should not drive mass evictions that reduce effective pool capacity for >2 minutes. Autoscaler should react within configured cooldowns without oscillatory overshoot.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route steady batched traffic to dedicated pool dp-eu-09 with multiple long-lived streams.
2) Trigger background KV cache compaction on 2-3 nodes (simulate snapshotter GC) and observe allocator decisions.
3) Observe attach attempts and autoscaler reaction in metrics/ui; watch p50/p99 for batched routes.
4) Repeat with different prefetch thresholds to see sensitivity.
investigation_notes: 09:10 - Initial hypothesis: background snapshotter GC triggered a cascade because eviction heuristic weights include recent IO pressure + prefetch footprint; observed high eviction scores on prefetched caches.
09:30 - Confirmed temporal alignment between snapshotter compactions and allocator eviction decisions on node-117, node-119, node-121.
09:45 - Autoscaler suppressed scaling: attach telemetry dropped while nodes were marked 'draining' causing delayed scale-up; cooldown prevented immediate new node allocation.
10:05 - Reproduced locally in staging by forcing GC on two nodes while running many long-lived small streams; observed similar short-term capacity dip and attach spikes.

10:20 - Hypothesis refinement: noisy-neighbor effect — one tenant's large prefetch pattern amplified GC frequency on nodes due to combined lease alignment; eviction scoring amplified the impact across the stripe.
11:00 - Mitigation trial: increased allocator eviction threshold and temporarily disabled automatic prefetch on affected pool; attach failures reduced and throughput recovered within ~8 minutes.

Follow-up actions: adjust eviction scoring to weight longitudinal footprint less during GC windows; add snapshotter->allocator backpressure signals; tune autoscaler to ignore transient attach drops shorter than 45s.

resolution: Mitigation applied: temporary eviction-threshold bump and disabled aggressive prefetch on dp-eu-09; capacity returned to near-baseline within ~8 minutes. Ongoing fixes: (1) patch allocator to accept snapshotter GC hints to avoid cascade, (2) add autoscaler resilience to transient attach drops <45s, (3) add knob to limit per-tenant prefetch concurrency on dedicated pools. Related PRs created and scheduled for staged rollout: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428. Postmortem and customer RCA to be published by 2026-03-18.
